newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest stock exchange turnover picks up.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest stock exchange turnover picks up.

text.p: Turnover on the Bucharest bourse rose strongly to 53.3 million lei on Tuesday from 31.2 million previously, with the increase backed by growing demand in several stocks rather than election results, traders said.
"The results of Sunday's polls did not seem to impress the market. Turnover grew under stronger interest in Azomures and several other stocks," said one trader.
Azomures SA fertiliser maker took 70 percent of total turnover and closed 100 lei stronger at 11,100.
Four stocks rose, three showed losses, three remained unchanged and three had no trade.

Syringe maker Sanevit SA was suspended from trading after the company last week requested a halt to its Tuesday trading to give it time to inform investors of decisions reached during a recent shareholders' meeting.
Investors also showed interest in Artrom SA engineering company, which had 5.0 million lei in turnover and traded more than 2,500 of the total 7,900 shares which changed hands on Tuesday.
Brokers said they did not expect a reinvigoration of trading in the immediate future on the back of poll results.
"The new government will have to work to encourage capital market growth and then we'll have revival," a broker said.
Reformist Emil Constantinescu won presidential elections at the weekend, defeating incumbent President Ion Iliescu.

Constantinescu's centrist Democratic Convention, which won parliamentary polls two weeks ago and will form a government, said the new cabinet would work to improve the emerging capital market by stepping up privatisation and stimulating investment.
Two unofficial value-weighted indices -- the VAB, computed by Vanguard SA securities, and Bucharest Investment Group 's BIG -- dropped from the previous session by 0.2 percent each.
